assertion_results.text: Data extraction correctly identifies CVE-2026-31812, library quinn-proto, affected range < 0.11.14, and fixed version 0.11.14 from the Vulnerability issue (Step 1)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Step 1 table: CVE ID = CVE-2026-31812, Vulnerable library = quinn-proto, Affected version range = 'versions before 0.11.14', Fixed version = 0.11.14. All four fields correctly extracted.

assertion_results.text: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as Cargo based on the library name and component context (Step 1 Ecosystem detection)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md lines 57-64: 'The vulnerable library quinn-proto is a Rust crate. The Ecosystem Mappings tables in both streams matrices list Cargo as the ecosystem for the backend repository, with Cargo.lock as the lock file.' Classification: 'Source dependency (Cargo)'.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the security-matrix.md supportability matrix — no versions are skipped (Important Rule 4)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md lists 7 versions across both streams: 2.1.0 (v0.3.8), 2.1.1 (v0.3.12), 2.2.0 (v0.4.5), 2.2.1 (v0.4.8), 2.2.2 (v0.4.9), 2.2.3 (v0.4.11), 2.2.4 (v0.4.12). All versions from both the 2.1.x and 2.2.x streams are present, including retag version 2.2.2 and non-affected versions 2.2.3/2.2.4.

assertion_results.text: Version impact analysis uses pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version, not branch HEAD (Important Rule 13)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md Build Tag column uses specific pinned tags: v0.3.8, v0.3.12, v0.4.5, v0.4.8, v0.4.9, v0.4.11, v0.4.12. affects-versions.md confirms lock file checks at pinned commits: 'git show v0.4.5:Cargo.lock', 'git show v0.4.8:Cargo.lock'. No branch HEAD references used.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table identifies retag versions and carries forward the affected status from the original version (Important Rule 5)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md line 13: '2.2.2 | 2.2.x | v0.4.9 | 0.11.12 | YES | retag of 2.2.1 (same as v0.4.8)'. Analysis section: 'Version 2.2.2 is a retag of 2.2.1 (build tag v0.4.9 is a retag of v0.4.8). The lock file check was skipped and the result carried forward from 2.2.1 (quinn-proto 0.11.12, affected).'

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction proposes replacing PSIRT-assigned versions with lock-file-verified versions, showing the diff (Step 3.2)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md lines 13-15 show the diff: 'Current: [RHTPA 2.0.0]' / 'Proposed: [RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2]'. Rationale explains RHTPA 2.0.0 is incorrect ('PSIRT assigned this version based on scan time, not actual dependency analysis') and each proposed version is justified with lock file evidence.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction references version names from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md uses version names throughout: 'RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2'. Lines 32-36 explain dynamic discovery: 'Jira versions matching prefix RHTPA would be discovered dynamically via getJiraIssueTypeMetaWithFields.' Planned Jira operation uses placeholders '<RHTPA-2.2.0-version-id>' rather than hardcoded IDs.

assertion_results.text: Remediation tasks include Repository, Target Branch, acceptance criteria, and dependency linkage between upstream and downstream tasks (Important Rule 9)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Task 1: Repository=backend, Target Branch=release/0.4.z, Acceptance Criteria with 4 checkboxes, Dependencies='Depends on: TC-8001'. Task 2: Repository=rhtpa-release.0.4.z, Target Branch=main, Acceptance Criteria with 2 checkboxes, Dependencies='Depends on: <dependency-bump-task-key>'. Task 3: Repository=backend, Target Branch=release/0.3.z, Acceptance Criteria with 3 checkboxes. Task 4: Repository=rhtpa-release.0.3.z, Target Branch=main, Dependencies='Depends on: <upstream-backport-task-key>'. Linkage sections document Blocks dependencies between downstream and upstream tasks.

assertion_results.text: For Cargo ecosystem, remediation creates two tasks: upstream backport task and downstream propagation subtask with Blocks dependency (Important Rule 8)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md creates 2 tasks per stream. Stream 2.2.x: Task 1 (dependency bump) + Task 2 (downstream propagation) with 'Downstream propagation task -> dependency bump task: Blocks link'. Stream 2.1.x: Task 3 (upstream backport) + Task 4 (downstream propagation) with 'Downstream propagation task -> upstream backport task: Blocks link'. Both streams follow the Cargo 2-task pattern with Blocks dependency.

assertion_results.text: The analysis presents triage recommendations as proposed actions — framing Affects Versions changes, label additions, and status transitions as proposals rather than executed mutations (Guardrails)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md line 18: 'No Jira operations were actually performed -- these are the planned actions only.' affects-versions.md line 37: 'Planned Jira Operation (not performed)', line 54: 'No Jira operations were actually performed.' remediation.md line 380: 'No Jira operations were actually performed -- all task descriptions and linkage plans are documented here for reference only.' Language throughout uses 'would be performed', 'Proposed:', 'would be posted'.

assertion_results.text: The data-extraction output describes Step 0.7 actions before the Step 1 data table: assigning the CVE issue to the current user and transitioning it to Assigned status (Step 0.7)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md lines 1-18 (labeled 'Step 0.8 -- Early Assignment Actions', before Step 1): describes (1) 'Assign TC-8001 to the current user' via jira.edit_issue with assignee, and (2) 'Transition TC-8001 from New to Assigned' via jira.transition_issue. Both actions appear before the Step 1 data table starting at line 22. Note: output labels this Step 0.8 rather than 0.7, but both required actions (assign + transition to Assigned) are present and positioned before Step 1.

assertion_results.text: Release orchestration preserves interactive confirmation of the exact release Epic version and separate child Task creation; when release evidence or confirmation is unavailable, it reports pending work instead of claiming creation.
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Step 7.5, lines 14-22: 'Engineer confirmation is required before creating the Epic. Options: 1. Accept RHTPA 2.2.5, 2. Specify a different version, 3. Skip release Jira for this stream.' Lines 24-28: 'If no release Task exists, prompt the engineer to confirm creation of RHTPA <version> CVE triage as a child of the release Epic.' The output preserves interactive confirmation gates and does not claim to have created any release Jira artifacts.

assertion_results.text: Release dedup is skipped when its Upstream Affected Component configuration is absent. When trusted release evidence is available, the proposed procedure resolves originating CVEs through Blocks/Depend links, compares their components and allows library-summary fallback only for a missing Depend link or component field; a known nonmatch does not count as dedup, and unavailable release evidence is not fabricated.
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Step 7.5.3, lines 34-37: 'The Upstream Affected Component custom field is not configured in the Security Configuration for this project. Therefore, the cross-CVE dedup check is skipped entirely.' Lines 49-52: 'Decision: No dedup applies. The Upstream Affected Component custom field is not configured in Security Configuration, so Step 7.5.3 cross-CVE dedup is skipped entirely.' No release evidence is fabricated; the output correctly skips dedup when the required configuration field is absent.
